problems.title: Final sampling prevents the claimed dimension-one rate
problems.source_location: Theorem 4.1, PDF p.6; Algorithm 2, PDF p.5, line 9
claim: Theorem 4.1 covers \(d=1\) and claims \(\widetilde O(dD\sigma^{1/d})\) error. Algorithm 2 ends by drawing \(m\) independent samples, with \(m\) of order \(\sigma^{-1}\) up to logarithmic factors.
analysis: Use target \(\mu=(\delta_0+\delta_1)/2\). For any candidate distribution on \([0,1]\), its independent empirical CDF at an interior threshold is \(K/m\), with \(K\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,p)\). For even \(m\), the symmetric convex expected deviation from \(1/2\) is minimized at \(p=1/2\) and equals \(\tfrac12\binom{m}{m/2}2^{-m}\asymp m^{-1/2}\). Integrating the CDF deviations over \((0,1)\) gives the same lower bound for \(\mathbb E W_1\), uniformly over the preceding candidate law and therefore also over its randomness. The prescribed sample count is of order \(\sigma^{-1}\) up to logarithms, giving a \(\sigma^{1/2}\) obstruction incompatible with the asserted dimension-one \(\sigma\) rate.
result: The theorem’s stated dimension-one conclusion fails for its own final sampling step. Dimensions at least two and other output algorithms are not refuted.
assumptions: The output consists of independent equally weighted samples; the theorem includes \(d=1\).
repair: The established balancing recurrence supports the exponent \(1/\max\{d,2\}\), yielding \(\widetilde O(dD\sigma^{1/\max\{d,2\}})\). Use integer sample counts and an iteration horizon controlling the residual term.
problems.impact_rationale: This directly contradicts the paper’s central convergence rate on an included dimension.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: A fixed-dataset accuracy premise cannot imply the packing bound
problems.source_location: Lemma 3.1, PDF p.5; Definition D.1, PDF p.17; proof, PDF p.28
claim: Lemma 3.1 states accuracy at a fixed dataset \(S\) and concludes \(\varepsilon\geq\log M(\Omega,\rho;2\eta)\). Its packing convention permits distances equal to \(2\eta\).
analysis: A mechanism that always returns that fixed \(S\) is perfectly private and perfectly accurate there, regardless of the larger domain’s packing number. Even uniform closed-ball accuracy permits the constant midpoint on \([0,1]\) when \(\eta=1/2\), since the endpoint accuracy balls touch. Uniform input accuracy and strict separation are therefore necessary for the proposed disjoint-event proof. Diameter and ambient dimension alone also do not lower-bound packing growth.
result: The lemma as quantified admits trivial counterexamples. A dimension-dependent interpretation additionally requires domain geometry.
assumptions: Accuracy is read with the printed fixed-input quantifier and closed accuracy balls.
repair: Require accuracy at every input and centers separated by more than \(2\eta\). The neighboring-dataset disjoint-event argument then gives \(\varepsilon\geq\log((M-1)(1-\tau-\delta)/\tau)\) under the stated error ranges.
problems.impact_rationale: The stated privacy lower bound fails under its own quantifiers; this is a substantive mathematical claim, not a code-only issue.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The histogram proposition can return a nonprobability measure
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, Proposition 4.1, PDF pp.7–8; Appendix H, PDF pp.26–28
claim: Proposition 4.1 normalizes retained noisy mass when positive and otherwise returns the zero histogram, then states an ordinary probability-measure \(W_1\) bound.
analysis: For one positive bin with \(n=1\), \(\varepsilon=1/2\), and \(\delta=0.1\), all mass is discarded with probability \(0.95\). The returned zero measure has total mass zero, so the asserted ordinary \(W_1\) quantity is undefined. The proof also omits absolute values on negative discarded noise. The simulation caller’s fallback and Algorithm 2’s simplex projection avoid this particular output defect and must remain distinct.
result: The proposition is not well-defined on its stated output branch. This does not show that Algorithm 2 returns a zero measure.
assumptions: \(W_1\) denotes ordinary Wasserstein distance between probability measures, not an independently defined unbalanced transport distance.
repair: On empty retained mass, return a probability distribution fixed on the public candidate support, then analyze the fallback probability and discarded absolute mass. This is probability-valued post-processing, with privacy conditional on the support’s provenance.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local proposition/proof-domain failure; the main algorithm has an explicit countercontrol.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The class-name selector uses position rather than dataset class identity
problems.source_location: Section 6, PDF p.9; Figures 3–4, PDF p.10; PE_cifar10_code.ipynb, cell 8
claim: The CIFAR notebook’s `Cifar10` selector iterates the length of the requested class-name list instead of resolving those names against the dataset class map.
analysis: A one-name dog request therefore selects class index \(0\), which is airplane, rather than dog index \(5\), while retaining dog metadata. The mismatch follows directly from the selector.
result: The release can mislabel the selected subset. Which historical code produced the published dog figures is unverified.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Resolve requested names through the dataset’s actual class map and keep a separate local subset label.
problems.impact_rationale: This release selector discrepancy does not establish a mislabeled published experiment.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
